To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
WB MRI including DWIMRI is feasible in follow up of patients with testicularcancer.
WB MRI with CT-MRI including DWI is feasible and accurate in the follow-up of patients after treatment of testicular cancer.
whole-body MRI including diffusion-weighted MRI is feasible in follow up of patients with testis cancer, and diffusion-weighted imaging may be used to assess the activity of residual mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an innovative and effective method for the treatment of patients with testicle cancer.
a new method of whole body imaging, which may be used as a complementary method in the follow-up of testis cancer patients.
the use of magnetic resonance imaging (WB MRI) in follow-up of cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of MRI in follow-up of the testicular cancer patients is feasible.
whole body MRI including DWI is a feasible imaging technique in follow-up of these patients.

the use of WB MRI in follow-up of cancer patients, including DWI, may contribute to a better management of these patients, but the clinical impact of these imaging techniques needs to be evaluated in a larger patient cohort.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of WB MRI with multi-step DWI may be useful in the follow-up of testis cancer patients, especially when 18F-FD PET/CT is not feasible.
WB MRI with CT and DWI can be used in follow-up of the patients with testicular carcinoma.
whole body MRI including DWI may contribute in future follow-up of patients treated for testicular cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WB MRI with DWI may be a useful imaging tool in the follow-up of patients who underwent chemotherapy or surgery for testicular cancer.
the use of WB MRI in follow-up of cancer patients is feasible, and may contribute to important additional information regarding the activity of the residual masses.
whole-body MRI including multi-step diffusion-weighted imaging is feasible in follow up of patients with testis cancer.
